result.topic_en: Euler interpolates an arc from the sines of its multiples. With four arcs this gives an approximation to π. With infinitely many arcs it gives the series Φ/2 = sin Φ − ½ sin 2Φ + ⅓ sin 3Φ − …, which he specialises to the Leibniz series and related series for π.
result.transcription:
[p. 166]
tur ſuitus, quoniam inde tantum approximationes pro menſura circuli ſuppeditantur. Interim tamen obſeruaſſe haud piguit, ſi tantum quatuor arcus accipiantur, qui ſint
$a=\Phi,\ b=2\Phi,\ c=3\Phi,\ d=4\Phi,$
fore ex ſolutione problematis
$\Phi=\frac{\sin.\Phi}{1}\cdot\frac{2.2}{1.3}\cdot\frac{3.3}{2.4}\cdot\frac{4.4}{3.5}=\frac{8}{5}\sin.\Phi-\frac{2}{5}\sin.2\Phi+\frac{8}{105}\sin.3\Phi-\frac{1}{140}\sin.4\Phi$
$-\frac{\sin.2\Phi}{2}\cdot\frac{1.1}{1.3}\cdot\frac{3.3}{1.5}\cdot\frac{4.4}{2.6}$
$+\frac{\sin.3\Phi}{3}\cdot\frac{1.1}{2.4}\cdot\frac{2.2}{1.5}\cdot\frac{4.4}{1.7}$
$-\frac{\sin.4\Phi}{4}\cdot\frac{1.1}{3.5}\cdot\frac{2.2}{2.6}\cdot\frac{3.3}{1.7}$
quae expreſſio eo propius ad veritatem accedit, quo minor capiatur arcus $\Phi$; interim tamen etſi ad quadrantem vsque augeatur, vt ſit $\Phi=\frac{\pi}{2}$, error non fit enormis; prodit enim $\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{8}{5}-\frac{8}{105}=\frac{32}{21}$, ſicque $\pi=3\frac{1}{21}$. At ſi ſumamus $\Phi=30^\circ=\frac{\pi}{6}$, fit
$\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{3}+\frac{8}{105}-\frac{1}{280}\sqrt{3}$, ſeu
$\pi=\frac{184}{35}-\frac{171\sqrt{3}}{140}$,
qui valor tantum aliquot particulis centies millesimis veritatis a vero differt. Verum miſſa hac ſpeculatione caſus aliquot, vbi arcuum propoſitorum $a, b, c, d,$ etc. certa lege progredientium numerus eſt infinitus, percurram.

Exemplum I.
§. 12. Progrediantur arcus a, b, c, d, etc. ſecundum ſeriem numerorum naturalium, ſicque
$a=\Phi,\ b=2\Phi,\ c=3\Phi,\ d=4\Phi,$ etc.
in infinitum, ex quorum ſinibus p, q, r, s, etc. veram longitudinem arcus $\Phi$ determinari oporteat.
Solutio

[p. 167]
Solutio ergo problematis pro hoc caſu ſuppeditat hanc aequationem:
$\Phi=\frac{\sin.\Phi}{1}\cdot\frac{2.2}{1.3}\cdot\frac{3.3}{2.4}\cdot\frac{4.4}{3.5}\cdot\frac{5.5}{4.6}\cdot$ etc.
$-\frac{\sin.2\Phi}{2}\cdot\frac{1.1}{1.3}\cdot\frac{3.3}{1.5}\cdot\frac{4.4}{2.6}\cdot\frac{5.5}{3.7}\cdot$ etc.
$+\frac{\sin.3\Phi}{3}\cdot\frac{1.1}{2.4}\cdot\frac{2.2}{1.5}\cdot\frac{4.4}{1.7}\cdot\frac{5.5}{2.8}\cdot$ etc.
$-\frac{\sin.4\Phi}{4}\cdot\frac{1.1}{3.5}\cdot\frac{2.2}{2.6}\cdot\frac{3.3}{1.7}\cdot\frac{5.5}{1.9}\cdot$ etc.
$+\frac{\sin.5\Phi}{5}\cdot\frac{1.1}{4.6}\cdot\frac{2.2}{3.7}\cdot\frac{3.3}{2.8}\cdot\frac{4.4}{1.9}\cdot$ etc.
omnia autem haec producta eundem reperiuntur habere valorem $=2$, ita vt ſit:
$\frac{1}{2}\Phi=\sin.\Phi-\frac{1}{2}\sin.2\Phi+\frac{1}{3}\sin.3\Phi-\frac{1}{4}\sin.4\Phi+\frac{1}{5}\sin.5\Phi-$ etc.
cuius ſeriei veritas caſu, quo angulus $\Phi$ eſt infinite paruus, per ſe eſt manifeſta. Evoluamus ergo caſus ſequentes.
1°. Sit $\Phi=90^\circ=\frac{\pi}{2}$, ac prodit ſeries Leibniziana
$\frac{\pi}{4}=1-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{9}-$ etc.
2°. Sit $\Phi=45^\circ=\frac{\pi}{4}$, orieturque haec ſeries:
$\frac{\pi}{8}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\ *-\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{7\sqrt{2}}\ *+\frac{1}{9\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{11\sqrt{2}}-$ etc.
quae reſoluitur in has duas:
$\frac{\pi}{8}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{11}-\frac{1}{13}-\frac{1}{15}+$ etc.)
$-\frac{1}{2}(1-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{11}+$ etc.)
ita vt ſit
$1+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{11}-\frac{1}{13}-\frac{1}{15}+$ etc. $=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}$.
3°. Sit $\Phi=60^\circ=\frac{\pi}{3}$, eritque
$\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\ *+\frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{5}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+$ etc.
ſeu
$\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}=1-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{7}-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{11}+$ etc.
4°.

items.quote:
Progrediantur arcus a, b, c, d, etc. ſecundum ſeriem numerorum naturalium, ſicque
$a=\Phi,\ b=2\Phi,\ c=3\Phi,\ d=4\Phi,$ etc.
in infinitum, ex quorum ſinibus p, q, r, s, etc. veram longitudinem arcus $\Phi$ determinari oporteat.
items.english: Let the arcs a, b, c, d, etc. proceed according to the series of natural numbers, so that a = Φ, b = 2Φ, c = 3Φ, d = 4Φ, etc. to infinity. From their sines p, q, r, s, etc., the true length of the arc Φ is to be determined.

items.quote: omnia autem haec producta eundem reperiuntur habere valorem $=2$
items.english: All these products are found to have the same value, = 2.

items.quote: qui valor tantum aliquot particulis centies millesimis veritatis a vero differt.
items.english: This value differs from the true one by only a few hundred-thousandth parts.
